Why do far infrared and microwave telescopes need cooling but radio telescopes don't?

They need chilling because otherwise the heat of the optics contaminates the picture. Infrared is heat and microwave is close enough.

Radio on the other hand is far enough away in spectrum it doesn't matter.

For infrared the bottom of the scale for what can be seen is based on the temp of the camera. So if it's in space, you have to make the camera a little colder than space so it can detect the heat from whatever. Source: my ass, mostly.

both of these replys are right.

Infrared radiation is just a fancy science word for heat. Microwave radiation is right next door on the electromagnetic spectrum (its why we use microwaves to cook our food). The sensor has to be kept as cold as possible in order for any signals it detects to not get lost in the "noise" from latent heat.
